mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate parent entity (e.g., Hong Kong holding company or Caribbean parent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Registrar of Companies of the parent entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For parent entities incorporated in Hague Apostille Convention member states: apostille from the parent jurisdiction's competent authority, then Chinese translation by a certified translation agency; do not add consular legalization. For parent entities in non-member states: chain of notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, then PRC Embassy/Consulate consular legalization in the country of origin, followed by Chinese translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active Status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar or corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention path: competent authority apostille (no consular legalization). Non-Convention path: notarization plus Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization plus PRC consular legalization. Must not chain apostille and consular legalization for the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution of the foreign shareholder authorizing WFOE incorporation and appointing the first legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate shareholder, notarized by a local notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarization, then apostille by the competent authority; then certified Chinese translation. Non-Hague: notarization, then foreign ministry legalization, then PRC consular legalization; then certified Chinese translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of the foreign shareholder (Memorandum and Articles of Association or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or authorized filing agent in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention: apostille by the competent authority. Non-Convention: consular legalization chain. Never stack apostille on top of consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Good Standing Letter from the foreign shareholder's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention member bank: notarize the signature, then apostille; then Chinese translation. Non-member jurisdiction: notarize, legalize by the foreign ministry, legalize by PRC consulate; then Chinese translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Resume or identity verification dossier of the proposed legal representative, directors, supervisors and senior managers (passport notarization and police clearance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local notary public and police authority in each individual's residential jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the person resides in an Apostille state: notarization plus apostille; no consular legalization. If the person resides in a non-Apostille state: notarization plus foreign ministry legalization plus PRC consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before engaging in WFOE preparation, the foreign shareholder, its beneficial owners, proposed directors, legal representative, supervisor, and all authorized signatories must undergo enhanced due diligence that includes: (i) screening against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK OFSI consolidated list, and the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list; (ii) determination of politically exposed persons (PEPs) covering domestic and foreign PEPs, immediate family members, and close associates, with enhanced continuous monitoring if any match is identified; (iii) adverse media review in both English and Chinese; (iv) verification of source of funds and source of wealth for any shareholder holding 25% or more; and (v) confirmation that no designated individual or entity appears in any PRC court judgment, tax enforcement blacklist, or market supervision blacklist.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) via State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) integrated 'One-Window Service' platform, with local Market Supervision Administration bureaus operating the enterprise name autonomous declaration module under the Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (SAMR Order No. 82, effective March 1, 2021).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered Chinese name must be composed of standardized Chinese characters; the name structure must follow the four-tier statutory sequence: [administrative division] + [distinctive trade name] + [industry or business characteristic] + [organizational form '有限公司']. The distinctive trade name must not contain two or more identical characters with any existing registered same-industry enterprise in the same jurisdiction; pinyin romanization is not a substitute for the statutory Chinese name unless paired with a separately registered English/corporate name. Proposed names must be screened against the Chinese character phonetic and stroke similarity standards, prohibited content rules, and the national negative list for enterprise names. An English name may be registered as a separate record but does not replace the mandatory Chinese legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR name autonomous declaration or pre-registration name verification is rejected, the applicant shall first review the electronic rejection reason issued by the local Market Supervision Administration through the enterprise registration one-window portal. Within 15 working days of the rejection, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration application to the same Market Supervision Administration through the portal, attaching the original proposed name, the rejection notice ID, the legal basis for the proposed name under the Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration, and any supplementary evidence showing the absence of identical or confusingly similar names. The bureau shall respond within 10 working days. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful or the bureau fails to respond, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration petition with the next higher Market Supervision Administration within 60 days of receiving the rejection or the expiry of the statutory response period, requesting a written decision together with all prior rejection correspondence and the name screening report. If the administrative reconsideration remains unfavorable, the applicant may initiate an administrative lawsuit before the competent People's Court within 6 months, but for practical incorporation timelines the applicant should concurrently file one or more backup names.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE engaged in export distribution of pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot base bricks under ISIC 4638, a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not permissible for the registered address because the PRC Company Law and the Market Entity Registration Regulations require a registered domicile that is a genuine, legally usable address capable of receiving legal documents and official correspondence. In practice, however, the registered address may be either an owned or leased physical commercial premises; many local SAMR bureaus accept address registration on a licensed incubator, government-sponsored entrepreneurship base, or a registered office service provider if such provider is on the local approved list. The critical limitation is taxation and banking: the local tax bureau and the foreign-exchange bank will require an actual business premises or a verifiable central office for on-site inspection during opening of bank accounts, issuance of VAT invoice quotas, and export tax rebate filing. A virtual mailbox alone will be rejected by the tax authorities for export tax rebate registration and by the bank for foreign exchange settlement and Letter of Credit negotiation. Therefore, for the hotpot base export distribution WFOE, the entity must lease a physical office and ideally a licensed food/condiment storage warehouse if it conducts any domestic purchase, storage, repackaging, or consolidation of export goods; if the WFOE operates as a pure trading/purchasing agent without domestic warehousing, a physical office suite with a lease agreement, property ownership certificate or title extract of the lessor, and a front-desk receiving arrangement is strongly recommended and is the practical benchmark for an unannounced physical inspection. The virtual office may only serve as an auxiliary executive mailbox, never as the registered address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: During the first 18 months after incorporation, the probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the local Market Supervision Administration, the tax bureau, or the customs/export rebate team is moderate to high, estimated at 65-75% if the WFOE applies for export tax rebates, general VAT taxpayer status, or Letter of Credit settlement. The inspection checklist includes: (i) the presence of the entity's nameplate at the registered address; (ii) lease contract in force with rent payment receipts; (iii) property ownership certificate or rental authorization of the lessor; (iv) desk, computers, files, stationery and staff presence; (v) tax registration certificate and electronic tax registration installed on site; (vi) a fixed telephone number and business card; (vii) warehousing or inventory records consistent with food additive/production license if applicable; (viii) safety and fire prevention documents; and (ix) a clean organization chart and employment records. If the entity is found vacant or the address is occupied by another enterprise, the SAMR may mark the entity as 'by address' through the 'address is not accessible' clause, revoke the tax registration, or treat the taxpayer as non-normal; the entity may then be listed as abnormal in the business blacklist, causing bank account freezing and cancellation of export refund qualification. To mitigate, the WFOE should maintain a nominal but physical office at the registered address with at least one employee or an appointed administrative representative physically available during business hours, and the lease term should be at least 12 months renewable.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory zero-fee registration under the PRC Company Law; official fees are waived by the State Council, but service fees may be charged by third-party agencies for document preparation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法) and its Enforcement Rules, particularly Articles 2, 4, 9, 10, 12, 18, 20, 47 to 50, 52, 54, 57, 61, 63, 90, 95, 129, 130, 132, 161, 171, 172, 192, 193, 201, 202, 207, 208, 210, 213, 225, 241, 253, 277, 387, 388, 390 and 391 to 395, together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and related investment and foreign exchange approval rules applicable to a wholly foreign-owned limited company incorporated in Taiwan.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, Company Registration Section, as the central competent registry authority for company incorporation and commercial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application Form (Application for Registration of a Company) filed through the Taiwan MOEA Company and Commerce Registration Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan prescribes no general statutory minimum paid-in capital for a limited company. The foreign investor must obtain a Foreign Investment Approval Letter before remitting capital, deposit the approved capital into a newly opened Taiwan bank account, and obtain a bank-issued capital balance certificate and, where required, a certified public accountant capital verification report for filing with MOEA. No blocked escrow account is statutorily required, but the paid-in capital must remain in the account and may not be withdrawn before the Company Registration Certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD. At a meeting of the Board of Directors held on the [ ] day of [ ], 20[ ], at [Registered Office], Taiwan, with a quorum of directors present and voting, the following resolutions were duly proposed, seconded, and unanimously adopted in accordance with the Taiwan Company Act, the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, and the Articles of Incorporation of CN_WFOE_LTD. RESOLUTION 1: SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUE. IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED that the initial registered and paid-in share capital of the Company shall be established in New Taiwan Dollars and shall be divided into shares with an aggregate par value sufficient for the approved investment amount. The Board ratifies the share subscription agreement executed by the foreign shareholder, directs the Chief Executive Officer to cause payment of the subscribed capital into a newly created capital deposit account at a licensed bank in Taiwan, and instructs that a bank certificate of capital balance and a certified public accountant capital verification report be obtained and filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the Taiwan Central Bank in compliance with the Foreign Investment Approval. RESOLUTION 2: BANK ACCOUNT AND SIGNATORY AUTHORIZATION. IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED that the Company shall open operating, foreign exchange, and tax deposit accounts at [Bank], Taiwan. The Board authorizes the Manager, the Finance Director, and such other named signatories, jointly or singly, to sign cheques, drafts, wire transfers, letters of credit, shipping instructions, customs declarations, and tax filings. All such authority is subject to the internal anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer policies of the bank and the Company, and the approved bank signatory specimen cards are adopted. RESOLUTION 3: REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [Full Address], Taiwan, and that the company seal, corporate records, and statutory registers shall remain in the custody of the Company Secretary and the designated director under a dual-custody arrangement. The Board directs the registration of the registered office address with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and all relevant government agencies. RESOLUTION 4: STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed Director and Chairperson, [Name] is appointed Manager and General Manager, [Name] is appointed Company Secretary, and [Name] or a licensed CPA firm is appointed Auditor. Each officer shall execute an acceptance declaration and shall have authority to represent the Company before the Ministry of Economic Affairs, National Taxation Bureau, Taiwan Food and Drug Administration, Bureau of Foreign Trade, Customs Administration, and local fire, environmental, and labor authorities. All officers shall take office with immediate effect, and the Board directs the filing of all officer appointments and consents within the statutory period. This resolution shall be binding and effective from [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Company Name Pre-Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC), Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Foreign Investment Application and proposed company name reservation through the MOEA One-Stop Service online portal. The application must set out the investment amount, the business scope of export distribution of pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot base bricks under ISIC 4638, the proposed English and registered company name, foreign shareholder identity documents, and the capital remittance plan. Confirm that the proposed wholesale and distribution activity is not on the restricted list under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals. The foreign investor must notarize all corporate and identity documents, obtain authenticated English translations where applicable, and await the formal Investment Approval Letter before remitting any capital into Taiwan.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Investment and business plan for ISIC 4638 food wholesaling and export distribution
Notarized certificate of incorporation and passport of the foreign investor
Certificate of shareholder authorizing the signatory or attorney-in-fact
Approved company name reservation form
Power of Attorney appointing the Taiwan formation agent
Bank and capital remittance plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, the investor shall respond within 30 days with amended or supplementary documents, pay any applicable administrative fee, and file an administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan within 30 days if the rejection is based on an erroneous classification of the business scope. If the objection relates to the food wholesale category, the applicant may resubmit a narrowed business scope limited to wholesale distribution without manufacturing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance, Bank Verification, and Company Incorporation Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, open the paid-in capital account at a Taiwanese bank and remit the approved foreign currency capital. Obtain from the bank a certificate of paid-in capital balance and, as required, engage a Taiwan certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report. Submit the Company Incorporation Registration Application through the MOEA Company Registration Portal, together with the articles of incorporation, director and manager consent letters, capital verification evidence, registered office lease or ownership proof, and corporate seal card. The MOEA Department of Commerce will review the filing and issue the Company Registration Certificate, thereby completing the statutory incorporation of the wholly foreign-owned limited company.
required_dossiers: Company Incorporation Registration Application Form
Articles of Incorporation with required Taiwan statutory provisions
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Bank capital balance certificate
Certified public accountant capital verification report
Passport or national ID copies of all directors and managers
Notarized lease or certificate of title for the registered office
Officer consent and acceptance declarations
Company seal or chop registration card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a query or suspension notice, the applicant shall deliver corrected or missing documents within 15 days, re-execute any defective resolutions or articles with unanimous shareholder consent, and request prompt re-review. If the capital verification is challenged, the applicant must replace the capital certificate and re-file within 30 days. If the registration is refused, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Foreign Exchange Registration, and Customs Export Code
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan and Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after issuance of the Company Registration Certificate, the Company must file tax and Uniform Invoice Number registration with the National Taxation Bureau and complete value-added tax, business tax, and any employer registrations. The Company shall also apply to the Customs Administration for a customs importer and exporter declaration code, which is mandatory for the planned Swift TT and Letter of Credit payment rails and for export documentation. The authorized bank will file the foreign exchange remittance registration with the Taiwan Central Bank under the foreign investment approval number. This step ensures that the Company is tax-compliant at entity level and can lawfully execute cross-border sales and customs declarations.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Unified Invoice Number application and tax registration form
Articles of Incorporation and incorporation resolution
Tax authority declaration of business address
Bank account ledger and bank seal card
Customs registration application form
Business license or registered office lease for tax address
Foreign exchange remittance approval letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is suspended due to an incomplete business address, the Company shall submit the current lease and municipal usage certificate within 15 days. If customs data are mismatched, the Company shall file a correction through the Customs Administrative Information System and provide purchase invoices, logistics contracts, and proof of export sales. Late or rejected registrations may be cured by administrative rectification and the payment of any penalty assessed under taxation rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taiwan Food Business Operator Registration and Foreign Trade Export License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA) and Bureau of Foreign Trade (BOFT), Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before conducting any distribution activity, the Company must register as a food business operator with the TFDA Food Business Registration System. Because the product is a pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot base brick intended for export under ISIC 4638 or NAICS 424490, the Company must also apply for the BOFT Exporter Registration Certificate and, where applicable, a food product export hygiene certificate. The Company shall maintain batch traceability records, label compliance documents, product composition specifications, and warehouse sanitary records. For export to mainland China, the Company must also satisfy cross-strait customs quarantine and pre-packed food labeling requirements, including proof that the free-sale certificate and product analysis are available.
required_dossiers: TFDA Food Business Operator Registration Application
Company Registration Certificate and Uniform Invoice Number certificate
BOFT Exporter Registration Application Form
Product composition, ingredient, and label dossier for spicy tallow hotpot base
Packaging material compliance certificate
Warehouse address and food hygiene storage plan
Batch traceability program and GHP or HACCP plan
Free sale certificate or product export license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If TFDA registration is queried, the Company shall submit corrected labeling or product composition documents within 20 days and may be required to conduct re-labeling at a compliant pre-packing facility. If BOFT suspends the export license for tariff classification reasons, the Company shall submit an ISIC and HS code justification and obtain a classification ruling from Taiwan Customs within 30 days. Any suspension may be cured by filing a written appeal and providing further product safety test reports.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Warehouse Civil Defense Fire Safety, Occupational Health, and Environmental Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Fire Bureau; Local Environmental Protection Authority under the Environmental Protection Administration; Local Labor Regulatory Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the physical warehouse used for storing and distributing the pre-packaged hotpot soup base bricks, the Company must obtain a fire safety and civil defense certification covering fire extinguishers, emergency exits, detection systems, and evacuation plans. The warehouse structure and racking system must pass a structural load inspection if shelving is installed. If refrigerated storage is used, the Company must apply for environmental registration for stationary refrigeration equipment and maintain refrigerant log records. If no manufacturing or chemical processing operations are conducted, no full environmental impact assessment report is required. The Company shall also register for occupational safety and health compliance and carry out a workplace self-inspection for manual handling and rail safety.
required_dossiers: Civil Defense Fire Safety Inspection Certificate
Fire extinguisher and alarm installation completion certificate
Structural load approval or certificate of professional engineer
Occupational safety and health self-inspection report
Environmental registration form for refrigeration equipment if applicable
Refrigerant type, charge amount, and leakage test records
Waste disposal and sanitation service contract
Emergency response and evacuation drill records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire bureau issues a non-compliance notice, the Company shall correct all fire safety defects and request re-inspection within 30 days. If the environmental registration is challenged, the Company shall file supplementary pollutant control and refrigerant compliance data with the local environmental protection authority within 30 days. Any labor or occupational safety violation may be cured by implementing a corrective action plan and paying fines, after which a new inspection may be scheduled.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Bureau of Foreign Trade (BOFT), and local municipal fire and environmental agencies
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operator Registration Certificate; Exporter Registration Certificate; Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate; Environmental Registration for Warehouse and Refrigeration Equipment

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan (Taiwan EPA) and local municipal environmental protection bureaus
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D low-impact environmental registration only for a non-manufacturing wholesale and distribution warehouse; full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required for ISIC 4638 pre-packaged food distribution, unless the facility installs stationary refrigeration units above regulatory thresholds or engages in food processing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing wastewater or point-source VOC emissions are generated from warehousing and distribution. Sanitary wastewater discharged to a municipal sewer shall meet Taiwan sewer standards or, where applicable, effluent limits approximating chemical oxygen demand of 100 mg/L, biochemical oxygen demand of 30 mg/L, and suspended solids of 30 mg/L. For regulated refrigeration equipment, refrigerant leakage shall be detected and repaired, and annual leakage reporting is required if the system contains more than 50 tons carbon dioxide equivalent of fluorinated greenhouse gases; any release of ozone-depleting substances above the regulatory de minimis threshold must be reported to the EPA. Hazardous waste, including waste cleaning solvent and used oil, must be stored in sealed labeled containers and removed by licensed waste transporters within 90 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil defense fire safety and fire prevention certification from the local fire bureau is mandatory for the warehouse, including installation of fire extinguishers, alarms, emergency lighting, and evacuation signage. Structural load inspection and shelf-stability certification are required for all racking systems. Workplace safety approval shall be obtained under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, covering manual handling, forklift operation, electrical safety, and emergency equipment. The Company must also register employees for labor insurance, health insurance, and pension contributions with the local competent authority before commencing operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), with online filing through the provincial Electronic Tax Bureau portals integrated with the national e-Tax system (central portal www.chinatax.gov.cn); export customs data are exchanged with the General Administration of Customs of the PRC (GACC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The China WFOE is incorporated with the State Administration for Market Regulation and receives a Business License containing the Unified Social Credit Code. Within 30 days after the Business License is issued, the WFOE must complete tax registration with the local STA office through the Electronic Tax Bureau or on-site service hall, thereby obtaining a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) identical to the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code. The next steps are: (1) register for VAT and determine small-scale vs general VAT taxpayer status; (2) complete the export tax refund/exemption filing with the STA after GACC customs registration; (3) register in the trade foreign exchange receipt system with a designated bank and SAFE by completing the Trade Foreign Exchange Receipts and Payments Registry; and (4) if cross-border e-commerce export fulfillment is used, complete the applicable cross-border e-commerce retail export supervision filing. For a foreign non-resident entity without a permanent establishment in China, China-source taxation is enforced through a PRC withholding agent, and the non-resident entity should obtain/confirm its foreign taxpayer identification number and include tax residence details in the withholding registration records; a separate TIN is not required for a WFOE because the WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; the PRC does not have a U.S.-style check-the-box election or statutory hybrid mismatch elections. A WFOE is automatically classified as a resident enterprise under the Enterprise Income Tax Law and is taxable on worldwide income at 25%. For VAT only, an eligible taxpayer may elect general VAT taxpayer status below the RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales threshold; once the threshold is exceeded, registration as a general VAT taxpayer is mandatory.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) administered by the STA
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration, with voluntary registration below the threshold; all limited liability companies must complete tax registration and obtain a TIN upon establishment regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices, including export sales invoices, must be issued in the STA’s digital invoicing platform or through an approved integrating system using the taxpayer’s digital certificate/electronic seal. Invoice metadata must be transmitted to the Golden Tax Phase IV system, which performs real-time reconciliation of issuance, declaration and payment data; the GACC and STA exchange export manifest data through the electronic port. Special VAT invoices and fully digitalized e-invoices carry a centrally issued invoice code, QR anti-counterfeiting code and must be filled using the STA-specified data schema. There is no mechanical paper fiscal stamping in mainland China, but the issuance right and invoice block are centrally allocated and any abnormal invoice triggers automatic tax-risk control.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported pre-packaged hotpot soup base is eligible for the PRC VAT zero/export-rebate regime when: (a) the seller is a VAT general taxpayer; (b) the goods are actually cleared by GACC and transported from the customs territory of mainland China to a destination outside that territory, including Taiwan as a separate customs territory; (c) the export sale is supported by a valid customs export declaration and purchase contract with an overseas buyer; (d) the sales proceeds are repatriated to China through a designated foreign exchange bank and reported; and (e) the input VAT chain relating to tallow, packaging materials, seasoning and logistics is supported by lawful special VAT invoices. The exported goods are not subject to output VAT at the point of export, and the residual input VAT is refundable or creditable under the export tax rebate procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration Form with customs release and electronic port data
Bill of Lading or multimodal transport document showing the Taiwan consignee and port of discharge
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank-issued foreign exchange receipt/export proceeds settlement voucher
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list
Export sales contract or purchase order for the pre-packaged hotpot soup base
VAT special invoice(s) for domestic input purchases and export sales-related invoicing records
Export tax refund/rebate declaration submitted through the STA e-Tax system with the customs declaration number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA cross-checks the customs declaration, invoice issuance, logistics documents and bank foreign exchange receipts against the export rebate claim. If zero-rated exports are found to be based on false customs declarations, forged FIRC/foreign exchange vouchers, circular invoicing, or non-repatriation of export proceeds within the prescribed 180-day FX repatriation period, the zero-rating is reversed, the refunded VAT is clawed back with daily late-payment interest of 0.05% of the unpaid tax, and a penalty of one to five times the fraudulently refunded tax may be imposed under the Law on the Administration of Tax Levying and Collection. Where criminal threshold for fraudulent export tax rebating or VAT invoice fraud is met, the case is referred for criminal prosecution; the retroactive assessment limitation is extended for fraudulent conduct and can be unlimited.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange-rate system with a current-account convertibility regime for genuine trade and service transactions. The RMB is convertible for trade settlements and ordinary service payments, but the capital account remains regulated. A CN WFOE established by a Taiwanese investor must obtain SAFE FDI registration before inbound equity capital is received; outbound profit remittances require an audited annual financial statement, a completed foreign exchange settlement and sale application, CIT tax clearance, and a prior SAFE foreign-exchange payment declaration. Registered capital funds received into the Foreign Exchange Capital Account cannot be freely used or converted; they must be settled on a pay-as-you-go basis, with banks testing the authenticity of the underlying expenses. The Taiwan leg is subject to opposite rules: Taiwan does not strictly control trade-related NTD conversion, but the mainland side requires bank verification of customs declarations, invoices, and logistics records. No automatic full conversion exists for capital account transactions such as intercompany loans or shareholder advances; those must be separately registered and covered by the SAFE framework. Profit repatriation is not barred but is effective only if the company can evidence real operations, tax filing, and statutory capital preservation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SAFE goods-trade monitoring system, the WFOE must repatriate export proceeds to a domestic foreign-currency account; trade receipts must normally be collected within the contract's payment term and, if outstanding beyond 90 days from the date of customs declaration, must be reported as delayed collection in the SAFE digital monitoring system. The former mandatory percentage-based surrender was abolished; the company may retain export income in foreign currency or sell it to the bank at the prevailing market rate. No percentage conversion quota is applied unless a specific bank internal policy or a tax collection cross-check requires a documentary explanation for retained balances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account plus Basic Operational Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Deposit Account (RMB) plus Export Foreign Currency Collection Account
Trade Finance and Letter of Credit Settlement Account
Secondary Operating Account for Payroll, Tax and Working Capital

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary account, and only marginally usable as a supplementary rail. Under the PRC Banking Supervision Law, overseas and internet electronic-money institutions (EMIs) are not licensed deposit-taking institutions and cannot open corporate accounts or hold SAFE capital account registrations for a mainland WFOE. SAFE-licensed cross-border payment institutions may digitize small-value open-account trade flows, but they must ultimately toll through a Tier-1 licensed bank and cannot handle FDI capital, L/C negotiation, FX derivatives, or large T/T settlement. Feasibility rating: Restricted / Supplementary Use Only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative or a locally resident director must appear physically at the Tier-1 bank branch for a face-to-face KYC interview and sign all account documents. Remote video verification alone is not accepted by mainland Tier-1 banks for a WFOE's basic deposit and foreign exchange accounts; consular proxy opening is not generally available. If the legal representative is outside China, a local director or senior manager may attend with an original notarized power of attorney authenticated by the PRC embassy, consulate or recognized notarization service in the jurisdiction where the POA is issued, together with an official Chinese translation, passport/ID, company seal, business license, and SAFE FDI registration certificate. The bank will also perform a site inspection of the registered office and warehouse before activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain obscured by a Hong Kong or British Virgin Islands intermediate holding company between the Taiwanese investor and the mainland WFOE, creating a shell intermediation red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified legal-entity extracts and LEI certificates for every entity in the ownership chain; notarized register of directors and shareholders of the SPV; audited financial statements of each intermediate; the SAFE FDI equity registration form; and statutory declarations from the ultimate beneficial owner confirming economic substance, physical offices, and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound registered capital remittance originates from a third-party jurisdiction or from an account other than the ultimate shareholder's own bank account, triggering a source-of-funds alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized corporate resolution and board minutes approving the investment; the original SWIFT MT103 transaction reference; a bank letter from the remitting bank certifying the remitter's identity and account ownership; source-of-wealth documentation for the beneficial owner including tax returns, pay records and bank statements; and a PRC legal opinion on the cross-border capital injection structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export trade documents for pre-packaged hotpot soup base show discrepancies between LC invoices, customs declarations, packing lists, HS codes and shipping records, raising a trade-based money laundering concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete export compliance binder containing the sales contract; signed LC or purchase order; customs export declaration; bill of lading; inspection release; CIQ or hygiene certificate; SC food production license; export food manufacturer registration; HACCP certificate; product laboratory analysis reports; and dated warehouse inventory and loading photographs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Account-opening KYC declares seasoning wholesale but the WFOE's cash flows or disbursements suggest catering, cash-intensive retail or undocumented storage operations inconsistent with the declared manufacturing/export model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three years of audited financial statements; payroll and social insurance registers; utility and lease invoices; ERP production reports; raw-material purchase contracts; proof of physical production site through insurance schedules or notarized survey; and a detailed business plan with ISIC 4638 revenue projection and sample purchase orders from Taiwanese importers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwanese/Hong Kong investor executes a contribution resolution and wires foreign currency, preferably USD or RMB, to the WFOE's dedicated Foreign Exchange Capital Account maintained at Bank of China or ICBC. The remittance instruction must include the SAFE purpose code for foreign direct investment capital injection and reference the WFOE name and underlying FDI contract. The receiving bank verifies against the SAFE FDI registration certificate and the PRC business license before crediting. After receipt, the bank applies pay-as-you-go capital settlement; each conversion into RMB is tested against the intended use, such as lease agreements, supplier invoices, payroll, tax payments or production overhead. A PRC-licensed certified public accountant issues a capital verification report after each tranche or at full paid-in capital; the report is filed with the market regulation authority and supports subsequent SAFE and industrial-commercial updates. Capital account funds cannot be freely on-loaned or transferred to third-country related parties without prior SAFE approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For procurement of tallow, spices, packaging and other inputs from overseas suppliers, the WFOE can settle through SWIFT MT103 T/T transfers after submitting the contract, proforma invoice, customs declaration and a bank foreign-exchange purchase application; for larger bulk trade, it may open an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit through Bank of China or ICBC, with documents examined under UCP600; for low-risk repeat deliveries, Documentary Collections (D/P at sight or D/A with tenor) are acceptable. On the export side, the same rails operate in reverse: a Taiwanese importer remits via SWIFT MT103 in USD or RMB, or issues an L/C naming the WFOE as beneficiary; the WFOE's advising/negotiating bank checks invoice, packing list, bill of lading, health certificate, certificate of origin and customs declaration. All receipts and payments must be reconciled in the SAFE goods-trade monitoring system; mismatching purpose codes, missing logistics proof or non-trade related narrative in the SWIFT field 70 will cause rejection or suspension.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable RMB-USD forward settlement-and-sale contracts executed with a licensed onshore bank, supported by documented export/import cash-flow exposure and SAFE trade-monitoring records.

FX swaps and RMB-USD cross-currency interest rate swaps covering principal and interest on a SAFE-registered external loan or shareholder advance, provided the underlying debt is registered and the derivative is executed with a domestic Tier-1 bank under its SAFE derivatives qualification.

Cross-currency swaps for long-term intra-group financing to align USD investor funding with RMB operational cash flows, subject to the bank's internal product approval, SAFE negative-list review and board-level derivative risk authorization.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore; the mainland WFOE may not execute or accept an NDF, so any NDF hedging must be centralized in the offshore parent in Taiwan or Hong Kong and must not be linked to the WFOE's capital or trade settlement accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise annual income tax return (annual EIT return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (regional taxation bureau of the registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window 1 May through 31 May following each calendar tax year; for an approved non-calendar fiscal year, within five months after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing triggers assessment by tax authority on available records, late-payment interest computed from the original due date at the Central Bank postal one-year deposit reference rate, plus a delinquency surcharge of up to 15% of assessed tax for continued delay; fraudulent failure may expose the operator to criminal sanctions and monetary penalties of two to five times evaded tax. If the delinquency is not cured within a six-month rectification order, the Ministry of Economic Affairs may revoke company registration and proceed to strike-off/liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and, where applicable, certified CPA audit report filed with the company registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each fiscal year, no later than 30 June for a calendar-year company; CPA-audited report to accompany filing where the audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by 30 June may subject the responsible person to an administrative fine of approximately USD 610 to USD 3,050 (NTD 20,000 to NTD 100,000) per year of default; after an uncured rectification order of more than six months, the MOEA may strike off the company from the company register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax and remuneration statement filing (withholding certificates and payee copies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (withholding section)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing by 31 January of the year following the payment year; payee statements distributed by 10 February (or the next business day if the deadline falls on a holiday)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subjects each withholding statement/document to a penalty of approximately USD 23 per return up to an aggregate cap of approximately USD 460 per case, plus collection of the unreported withholding tax with late-payment interest; repeated defaults may trigger an audit and administrative strike-off referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders meeting and approval of annual financial statements, earnings appropriation and discharged directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (through submission of meeting minutes and any registered resolutions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting must be convened no later than 30 June following the fiscal year end; resolutions affecting registration must be filed within 15 days of the resolution date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The responsible person may be fined approximately USD 310 to USD 1,530 (NTD 10,000 to NTD 50,000) for failure to convene; if the meeting and financial acknowledgement remain outstanding after an MOEA rectification order for more than six months, the company may be administratively struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign investment status and operations report under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the foreign-invested company's fiscal year end, i.e., by 30 June for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual report may result in suspension or withdrawal of the foreign investment permit, blocking of profit remittance or capital repatriation applications, and administrative order to regularise; continued suspension for six months can lead to revocation of the WFOE registration and strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Taiwan-registered WFOE is required to have its annual financial statements independently audited and reported on by a licensed certified public accountant if any one of the following triggers is present at the fiscal year end or within the fiscal year: (1) paid-in capital equals or exceeds NTD 30 million (approximately USD 915,000); (2) annual operating revenue exceeds NTD 100 million (approximately USD 3.05 million); (3) balance-sheet total assets exceed NTD 300 million (approximately USD 9.15 million); (4) average monthly headcount exceeds 100 employees; (5) the company is a public company, financial holding company, bank, insurance, securities or futures enterprise, or is otherwise designated by MOEA or a sector regulator; (6) the company is required to produce consolidated financial statements under IFRS for its foreign parent. A non-public WFOE below these thresholds must still keep statutory books and prepare annual financial statements but is not statutorily required to have a CPA certification unless lender, shareholder, or MOEAIC conditions impose one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under the Business Entity Accounting Act, the Business Entity Accounting Handling Regulations and the Company Act, on an accrual basis with records maintained in New Taiwan Dollars (or a prescribed functional currency). Consolidating public companies apply Taiwan IFRS; non-public companies may elect Taiwan IFRS or the applicable domestic SME accounting framework/ROC GAAP as accepted by the Ministry of Economic Affairs. For this multinational WFOE, the statutory statements must be reconcilable to the parent's IFRS consolidation and the EIT return must separately follow the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a separate calendar-year UBO renewal declaration when no ownership change occurs; however, the beneficial ownership and 10% or more shareholder information must be filed in the MOEA central database within 15 days after incorporation or within 15 days after any transfer or change. At each annual shareholders meeting held no later than 30 June, the company secretary must reconfirm the register of members, the register of directors and beneficial ownership details, and record the confirmation in the minute book. Shareholding transfers are effective in the register on the transfer date and must be reported within the 30-day compliance window; any failure to update is a regulatory violation that can trigger MOEA rectification orders, administrative fines, and suspension of share transfer or dividend processing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders meetings and directors meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,800 per annum for a licensed registered office, corporate secretarial filing agent and annual maintenance service in Taiwan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 8,500 per annum for a low-risk non-public WFOE engaged in pre-packaged hotpot soup base wholesale distribution, assuming standard turnover, simple IFRS reconciliation and no regulatory review

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% unified Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) on the taxable income of the Chinese-resident WFOE; the Taiwan parent is a non-resident enterprise subject to withholding tax on China-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Low-Profit Enterprise concession: if taxable income is not more than RMB 3 million, employees do not exceed 300 and total assets do not exceed RMB 50 million, the effective CIT rate is 5% (25% of taxable income taxed at the 20% reduced rate). No general tax holiday applies to an export wholesale distributor of pre-packaged hotpot soup base; the Western Region Encouraged Industry 15% rate applies only if the WFOE is registered in a covered western province and the activity qualifies under the encouraged industry catalogue; the 100% additional R&D deduction is generally not available to a pure trading entity.
